rationale: C24 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Its unusually specific formulation concerning lands required for the “proper care, management, and protection of the objects of geological and scientific interest” closely parallels the child’s finding that lands were “no longer necessary for the proper care and management of the objects of scientific interest on the lands within the monument.” Both proclamations then use the 1906 act to alter monument boundaries, describe the affected land, and regulate its status under the public-land laws. The child reverses C24’s expansion logic, but that adaptation does not defeat the evident drafting relationship. C03 is the strongest structural alternative because it redefines an Alaskan national monument through numbered findings and operative clauses and amends the prior proclamation accordingly. C09 is relevant to the child’s separate national-forest restoration machinery but shares less distinctive language and a less similar overall form.

shared_material.child_excerpt: are no longer necessary for the proper care and management of the objects of scientific interest on the lands within the monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: are required for the proper care, management, and protection of the objects of geological and scientific interest located on lands within the said monument
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, closely corresponding language addressing whether particular lands are needed to manage and protect the monument’s scientific objects.

shared_material.child_excerpt: under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906 ... do proclaim ... that all of the following-described lands ... are hereby excluded from the Glacier Bay National Monument
shared_material.parent_excerpt: under and by virtue of the authority vested in me by section 2 of the act of June 8, 1906 ... do proclaim that ... the areas ... are ... added to and reserved as part of the Channel Islands National Monument
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same proclamation machinery to alter a national monument’s geographic scope, with the later directive adapting an enlargement template to an exclusion.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The lands in the above-described Gustavus Area shall not be subject to application, location, settlement, entry, or other forms of appropriation under the public land laws
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the areas ... are withdrawn from all forms of appropriation under the public-land laws
shared_material.explanation: Both attach a public-land-law withdrawal or non-appropriation rule to lands affected by the monument-boundary action.
